title: August and the Safehouse
premise: Ada Underhill, a financial-crimes investigator who faked her own death five years ago to escape the Voss Syndicate, is living quietly under a new name when a burner phone arrives with a voice she buried: Marcus Hale, her former partner, presumed dead. He warns that the syndicate, now laundering money through the very regulatory agency Ada works for, has scheduled a catastrophic 'accident' at a London data hub to erase evidence and kill a whistleblower. As Ada races to stop it, she discovers Hale's warning is bait in a power struggle inside the syndicate itself, and that her own survival was purchased with a betrayal she doesn't remember making. In the end, Ada must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the few people who stayed loyal to the woman she used to be; she stops the attack but burns her clean life forever, walking out of the ashes as the person she spent five years pretending not to be.
about_author: Felix Delacroix is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing dirty money through European banks before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers from a small flat in Lisbon, where he insists the coffee is better than the conspiracies.

chapters.title: The Clean Money
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Five years into her new life, Ada audits a shell company so bland it feels like a taunt, then comes home to find a burner phone in her mailbox with no sender. The emotional beat: the itch of a past that refuses to stay dead.

chapters.title: A Voice from the Water
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The phone rings at 3 a.m.; Marcus Hale's voice says her real name for the first time in five years and gives her an address and a deadline: nine days. She tells herself it's a scam. Emotional beat: terror disguised as skepticism.

chapters.title: Rules That Rewrite Themselves
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At work, Ada notices her own agency flagged one of the shell companies as 'cleared' by a signature that shouldn't exist. Her supervisor, Priya Nair, deflects too smoothly. Emotional beat: the ground tilting beneath institutional trust.

chapters.title: The Address
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She stakes out Hale's address and finds it's a syndicate safehouse, watched by men she recognizes from her old life. One of them looks directly at her car and smiles. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing she's the quarry.

chapters.title: What I Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Ada's POV. Five years earlier: the botched operation, the fire on the Thames, the moment Ada chose to disappear rather than testify. Emotional beat: guilt with teeth, revealing she left someone behind.

chapters.title: Priya
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya meets privately with a syndicate lawyer, revealing she's compromised but not corrupt—her sister's debts are the leash. She flags Ada's queries anyway. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada breaks into an archived case file and finds the syndicate's project codename—CLEAN SWEEP—and a date matching Hale's deadline. A data hub, an 'accident,' a whistleblower inside. Emotional beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. We meet Tomas Reyes, a mid-level syndicate accountant who copied ledgers and is hiding in plain sight. He doesn't know his name is already on CLEAN SWEEP's casualty list. Emotional beat: dramatic irony tightening like wire.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada finally corners Hale at a rail yard. He claims he's been undercover inside the syndicate since the fire, and that he called her because she's the only investigator they can't predict. Emotional beat: relief and suspicion in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Ledger Trap
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale admits the meeting was partly staged—he needed Ada seen with him to flush out the syndicate's mole in her agency. Ada realizes she's a pawn again. Emotional beat: betrayal wearing the mask of necessity.

chapters.title: Clean Sweep
chapters.summary: Syndicate POV via Viktor Sarn, the operations chief. Sarn explains the plan: a gas 'accident' at the Meridian Data Hub will destroy the ledger copies and kill Reyes, pinning blame on a disgraced contractor. Emotional beat: banality of monstrousness.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada tries to go through channels and is stonewalled at every level—the corruption reaches her directorate. She goes off-grid, burning her cover identity's paper trail. Emotional beat: grief for the life she's dismantling with her own hands.

chapters.title: The Man Who Smiled
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The watcher from Chapter 4 finds Ada and offers her a deal: walk away, and her old record stays dead. He reveals a fragment of what really happened the night of the fire—that Hale gave the syndicate her name. Emotional beat: the floor giving way.

chapters.title: Reyes Runs
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes senses the net closing and bolts with his ledger copies, calling the only number he trusts: the anonymous tip line that routes, unknowingly, to Ada's old handler. Emotional beat: panic, resourcefulness, doomed hope.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada intercepts Reyes first and hides him. Reading his ledgers, she finds the final piece: the attack isn't just destruction—it's insurance fraud layered over murder, signed off by someone inside her agency. Emotional beat: purpose sharpening into fury.

chapters.title: What Hale Gave
chapters.summary: Flashback, Hale's POV. The truth of the fire: Hale traded Ada's name to save his own family, believing the syndicate would only scare her. His guilt has driven his undercover years since. Emotional beat: cowardice examined honestly, forgiveness left unresolved.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada and Hale reconcile just enough to plan: get Reyes and the ledgers out through the data hub's maintenance tunnels before Sarn's crew seals them. Priya, wracked with guilt, feeds Ada the building's security rotations. Emotional beat: fragile alliance, borrowed time.

chapters.title: The Hub
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs intercut. Infiltration night: Ada and Reyes move through the tunnels while Sarn's team primes the gas systems and Hale draws the watchers. Everything runs two minutes ahead of schedule. Emotional beat: dread accelerating into motion.

chapters.title: Accident Pending
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. They're discovered; Reyes is shot covering Ada's escape with the ledgers. Ada triggers the gas alarms herself, forcing an evacuation that makes Sarn's 'accident' impossible without mass casualties he can't hide. Emotional beat: sacrifice converting horror into exposure.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Sarn corners Ada in the server hall; Hale arrives and takes the bullet meant for her, dying as sirens flood the building. Ada escapes with the ledgers and Reyes alive but critical. Emotional beat: victory purchased at full price.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Weeks later, Ada testifies—not as her cover identity, but as Ada Underhill, resurrecting her real name publicly. Priya cooperates; Sarn falls; the agency bleeds. Emotional beat: truth as both wound and weapon.

chapters.title: August
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, epilogue tone. In August, Ada visits Hale's unmarked grave and Reyes recovering by the sea. Another burner phone sits in her pocket—this time, she bought it herself. Emotional beat: survival redefined; she chooses to keep watching.
